fields.title: A demo is not a product tour
fields.keyTakeaway: Show how this specific client's problem gets solved using their data and their terms. A broad feature tour is remembered as "a lot of stuff" and gives no compelling reason to buy.
fields.checkQuestion: A client asked to see the product. What do you need to find out before the demo?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **how to demo the product to increase deal conversion?** A demo is about recognition, not completeness.
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you do not answer the question.** The salesperson walks through menu items. The client sees a complex system to learn and fails to see their problem addressed. After the call, they cannot articulate why they need it.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Four steps, three of them before the meeting
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Uncover the problem** — a brief pre-demo conversation: what exactly is broken right now and what does it cost in numbers.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Prepare data** — their SKU catalog, warehouse layout, internal naming. A demo built on "Item 1, Item 2" shows zero prep work.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Walk through one complete scenario** — start to finish, edge case included.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Establish a next step** — what happens next and when. A demo without a next step ends in radio silence.
fields.blocks/3/text:
First demo: thirty minutes through sections — receiving, putaway, dispatch, reports, permissions, integrations. The client said thanks and went silent.

Second demo: asked about pain points beforehand. Answer: "SKU mix-ups during dispatch cost us around 90 thousand a month." Uploaded their catalog and demoed exactly one scenario: order picking with a barcode scanner and handling a wrongly picked item.

The demo took twelve minutes. The contract was signed three weeks later.

The features shown were identical.
fields.blocks/3/title: Kedr: two demos in the same week
fields.blocks/4/text: A demo where everything runs perfectly breeds skepticism in anyone with real warehouse experience. Demonstrating error handling builds far more trust than a smooth happy path.
fields.blocks/4/title: Show the messy edge case too
fields.blocks/5/text: A demo does not replace a trial: it shows that the problem is solvable in principle, not how the product handles real volume in end-user hands. And it fails completely if the problem was misidentified — you will just end up convincingly demonstrating the wrong thing.
